originalPrompt: Consider a robot in 2-D with initial estimated position and covariance are μ₀=[2,2]ᵀ, Σ₀=[[0.25,0],[0,0.16]]. The robot receives a control input corresponding to a displacement of uₜ=[2,1]ᵀ with motion-noise covariance Vₜ=[[0.5,0],[0,0.4]]. Assume F=I, G=I, what is the predicted belief?
originalSourceText:
Q.7   Consider a robot in 2-D with initial estimated position and covariance are
                    𝝁𝟎= [2   , 𝚺𝟎= [0.25   0                                     2]       0    0.16]
      The robot receives a control input corresponding to a displacement of
                           𝒖𝒕= [2                                             1]
       with motion-noise covariance
                         𝑽𝒕= [0.5  0                                    0   0.4]
     Assume 𝐅= 𝐈, 𝐆= 𝐈, what is the predicted belief?

                    0      (A) 𝒩([4   , [0.5              3]  0   0.4])
                     0      (B) 𝒩([4   , [0.75              3]   0    0.56])
                     0      (C) 𝒩([2   , [0.75              2]   0    0.56])

                     0      (D) 𝒩([4   , [0.25              3]   0    0.16])
       Explanation: The predicted mean is
                               𝝁̅𝒕= [2 + [2 = [4                                        2]   1]    3]
     And the predicted covariance is
                     𝚺̅𝒕= [0.25   0  + [0.5  0 = [0.75   0                        0    0.16]   0   0.4]    0    0.56]
                         0       So, 𝒙𝒕~ 𝒩([4   , [0.75                  3]   0    0.56])
      Refer Slides-20, 21 of Lecture 44: Understanding the Perception and Localization
